purpose: Validate the V5 paired-execution and ground-truth protocol on six distinct verification shapes before scaling to the full 30-50 task corpus.
selection_rules: Upstream fix must be merged into the canonical repository.
The pre-fix revision must be pinned to the pull request base SHA.
The accepted fix must include a narrow regression witness or equivalent deterministic oracle.
The task must expose a materially different verification shape from the other pilot tasks.
No pilot selection record is treated as a ShowMeWhy benchmark result until paired baseline and ShowMeWhy runs are executed and independently labelled.

tasks.task_prompt: Investigate and fix pytest MonkeyPatch.setattr()/undo() so patching an inherited instance attribute restores the target to its original state. Preserve correct behaviour for inherited non-data descriptors, methods, direct instance attributes, properties/data descriptors, and slots. Inspect custom attribute-assignment machinery as an explicit boundary and surface any limitation rather than assuming ordinary __dict__ storage. Add focused regression coverage.
tasks.reproducer_command: python -m pytest testing/test_monkeypatch.py -k 'undo_inherited_attribute_on_instance or undo_inherited_non_data_descriptor_on_instance or undo_inherited_method_on_instance or undo_own_attribute_on_instance or undo_data_descriptor_on_instance or undo_slot_attribute_on_instance'
tasks.expected_pre_fix: Undoing a patch to an inherited instance attribute can leave a new instance __dict__ entry; an inherited non-data descriptor can become shadowed/frozen.
tasks.expected_post_fix: The accepted regression cases restore ordinary inherited lookup/storage semantics without leaving inherited values on the instance, while direct instance values, data descriptors and slots retain their expected behaviour. Custom attribute-assignment machinery remains a scrutiny boundary rather than an assumed guarantee.
tasks.boundary_notes: Review explicitly identified custom __setattr__ / proxy-backed storage as a regression risk for the proposed storage model before a later approval. The merged regression patch does not add a dedicated custom-__setattr__ test, so V5 must surface this as a boundary instead of claiming the upstream oracle proves it safe.

tasks.task_prompt: Investigate a mismatch between Pydantic validation behaviour and generated validation JSON Schema when a field has an alias but validate_by_alias=False. Make the validation schema describe keys the model actually accepts, preserve serialization behaviour, and verify nested model configuration remains correctly scoped. Add focused regression coverage.
tasks.expected_pre_fix: The validation JSON Schema exposes the alias even though validation with validate_by_alias=False rejects that alias and accepts the field name.
tasks.expected_post_fix: Validation schema keys match accepted validation inputs, serialization schema behaviour remains unchanged, and nested model configuration stays locally scoped.
tasks.boundary_notes: Serialization alias behaviour is intentionally out of scope because changing serialize_by_alias default semantics would be a broader compatibility decision; the pilot must not incorrectly claim that asymmetry was fixed.

tasks.task_prompt: Investigate pytest.warns handling of unmatched warnings when module-based warning filters are active. Reproduced warnings must be attributed consistently with their original location rather than spuriously matching the warnings module. Add a regression test that distinguishes the incorrect attribution from the intended behaviour.
tasks.expected_pre_fix: An unmatched warning re-emitted by pytest.warns is attributed to module 'warnings', causing module filters to match the wrong warning source.
tasks.expected_post_fix: Re-emitted warning attribution is derived from its filename/location, so a filter targeting module 'warnings' does not spuriously swallow it and a filter targeting the originating location can match it.
tasks.boundary_notes: warnings.WarningMessage does not retain the original explicit module string, so the accepted behaviour derives attribution from filename rather than claiming perfect reconstruction of unavailable provenance.

tasks.task_prompt: Investigate FastAPI SSE event formatting for payloads containing trailing newlines, CRLF/lone CR line endings, and Unicode characters that Python str.splitlines() treats as separators but the SSE protocol does not. Make formatting comply with SSE line-termination semantics and add boundary-focused regression tests for data and comments.
tasks.expected_pre_fix: SSE formatting drops trailing empty data/comment lines and incorrectly splits payloads on non-SSE Unicode/control line separators accepted by Python str.splitlines().
tasks.expected_post_fix: Only SSE-defined line terminators (LF, CRLF, CR) split event data/comments, trailing empty lines are preserved, and unrelated Unicode/control separators remain payload content.
tasks.boundary_notes: The discriminating counterexamples are trailing newlines plus U+2028 and vertical-tab payloads: a naive splitlines-based implementation can appear correct on ordinary LF input while still violating the SSE grammar.

tasks.task_prompt: Investigate FastAPI SSE and JSONL streaming endpoints that return HTTP 200 even when the route declares another status code or a dependency sets Response.status_code, while generated OpenAPI describes the declared response. Align runtime streaming behaviour with the existing response-status semantics without changing the default 200 case, and add control and OpenAPI consistency tests.
tasks.expected_pre_fix: SSE/JSONL streaming endpoints return 200 despite a declared or dependency-set status code, while OpenAPI can document the non-200 code.
tasks.expected_post_fix: SSE/JSONL streaming honours declared and dependency-set status codes consistently with raw StreamingResponse, default behaviour remains 200, and generated OpenAPI stays aligned with runtime semantics.
tasks.boundary_notes: Raw StreamingResponse is the existing control path and the default-200 case is a non-regression obligation; a fix that only changes documentation or only declared route codes is insufficient.

tasks.task_prompt: Investigate Ruff SIM117 false negatives for nested with statements when a combinable nested pair sits below an incompatible sync/async parent or an exempt context manager. Preserve top-to-bottom fixing for genuinely combinable parents, avoid invalid sync/async combinations, and add regression cases covering the relevant boundaries.
tasks.expected_pre_fix: SIM117 can suppress a valid nested-with diagnostic merely because a single-statement parent exists, even when parent/current cannot be combined due to sync/async mismatch or an exemption boundary.
tasks.expected_post_fix: Parent deferral occurs only when parent/current are genuinely combinable; valid nested pairs beneath incompatible boundaries are detected without proposing invalid cross-sync/async combinations.
tasks.boundary_notes: The accepted PR's ecosystem run surfaced additional real-project SIM117 findings, but the pilot oracle is the deterministic regression fixture/snapshot; ecosystem impact is supporting evidence, not the ground-truth label itself.
